validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: beyond doubt. Atlantic Bridge Phase I is the first tranche of the FERC-certificated Atlantic Bridge Project (Docket No. CP16-9-000; pre-filing docket PF15-12-000 opened January 30, 2015), an expansion of Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC's and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, LLC's existing systems into New England and the Canadian Maritimes. FERC issued the certificate order January 27, 2017 (RTO Insider, dated 2017-01-30, Wayback capture, reporting FERC approval of the project). Enbridge's own (then-current) project page states: 'The first phase of Atlantic Bridge, providing 40,000 dekatherms per day of incremental firm transportation service, began operating in November 2017.' EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset carries this exact project as 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' with status='Completed' in every one of 28 dated releases from 2018-05 through 2026-08, year_in_service_date=2017, operator='Algonquin Gas Transmission'. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission'/'Gas' is correct - an interstate natural-gas capacity-expansion project (compression + limited pipe replacement) on Algonquin's mainline, not gathering or distribution. DUPLICATE/CLUSTER CHECK (roster scan per the cluster warning): P0144 Access Northeast (cancelled, a much larger bundled compressor/lateral proposal tied to New England electric-utility RFPs) and P6011 Project Maple (2023 open-season proposal, still pre-FERC-filing/proposed) are both Algonquin/Enbridge New England expansion projects but are physically and temporally distinct from Atlantic Bridge - different scope, different capacity figures, different status - confirmed via P6011's own shard, which already adjudicated no duplicate/revival relationship. P7821 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase II' is Atlantic Bridge's own second tranche (93 MMcf/d, in-service January 2021 with the Weymouth compressor station) - correctly a SEPARATE row per GEM's segment-level convention, not a duplicate of P7820, but see the spec concern below for a value-swap between the two rows. System rows P0149/P0150 (the whole Algonquin/Maritimes & Northeast system) were swept in slice 1 and are out of this row's scope. No portfolio/system total has been read onto this segment row (Equitrans-precedent check): all capacity, length and cost figures cited here are Phase-I-specific, cross-checked against Phase II's different figures on the sibling row.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records LengthKnown=6.00 mi on P7820 (Phase I), but every source checked points to this being a value swapped with sibling row P7821 (Phase II), which currently records LengthKnown=0.00 mi. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset is completely consistent on this across ALL 28 dated releases from 2018-05 through 2026-08: 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' carries miles=0 (diameter and cost blank) in every single release, while 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 2' carries miles=6.3, pipeline_diameter_inches=42, cost_millions=451.8 in every release from 2019-01 onward (Aug-2026 release: Phase 1 = Historical Projects (1996-2024) sheet, Excel row 871, miles=0; Phase 2 = same sheet, Excel row 1014, miles=6.3/diam=42/cost=451.8). This is not a one-off data artifact - it is a stable, repeated distinction EIA has drawn for seven years. It is corroborated operationally by Enbridge's own (2019) project page: 'The first phase of Atlantic Bridge, providing 40,000 dekatherms per day of incremental firm transportation service, began operating in November 2017. When the project facilities in New York are completed and placed into service, we will have full project capacity available from New Jersey to Massachusetts.' This explicitly states that Phase I went into service in Nov 2017 WITHOUT the New York pipe-replacement facilities being complete - i.e., Phase I's capacity was delivered without any new pipe, consistent with EIA's Phase-1 miles=0. The physical pipe scope in question - originally 18.1 mi across several replacement/loop segments in the 2015 pre-filing notice (FR Doc 2015-11409), narrowed by the 2016 EA (FR Doc 2016-10674) to 4.0 mi of 42-inch replacing 26-inch in Westchester County, NY plus 2.3 mi of 42-inch replacing 26-inch in Fairfield County, CT (= 6.3 mi total, matching EIA's Phase 2 figure exactly), alongside the new Weymouth compressor station in Norfolk County, MA - was completed later. Enbridge's 10-K (FY2020, SEC EDGAR accession 0000895728-21-000010) states the Weymouth compressor station was 'brought online' in January 2021, 'the third and final phase of Atlantic Bridge' reaching the full 133 mmcf/d - and P7821's OWN recorded StartYear1=2021/StartMonth1=1 already matches this exactly, while P7821's SegmentCost=451,800,000 USD already matches EIA's Phase 2 cost_millions=451.8 exactly. In other words: P7821 already carries the correct cost and start date for the phase that includes the 6.3 mi/42-inch pipe, but has LengthKnown=0 (wrong) where P7820 has LengthKnown=6.00 (also wrong) - a clean two-row value swap, not an isolated error. Filed as a cross_row_lead for P7821 as well. Diameter is correctly left blank on this row once Length=0, per the standing rule that an expansion with no new physical pipe carries Diameter=blank.

Secondary/unresolved lead, not staged as a validity concern: Enbridge's FY2020 10-K describes Atlantic Bridge in THREE tranches - Phase I (Nov 2017, this row), a 'second phase' the 10-K says was 'placed into service in the second and fourth quarters of 2019', and 'Phase III' (the Weymouth compressor, fully commenced Jan 2021). GEM/EIA track only two phases (P7820, P7821), and P7821's own StartYear1=2021/Month1=1 matches the 10-K's 'Phase III'/Weymouth date, not the 2019 'second phase' date. It is possible the 2019 tranche is just a partial-capacity milestone within what GEM calls Phase II (not a separate project requiring its own row), but I could not confirm this either way this session (web-search budget was exhausted before I could chase the 2019 in-service claim further). Flagging for whoever next works this cluster to check whether a Q2/Q4-2019 partial-service milestone needs a StartYear2/StartYear3 entry on P7821, or is adequately covered by leaving it as one 2021 in-service date.
